title: Table, index and segment-text sizes
question: How large are D3's tables and indexes at run scale, and what share does kb.segment.text take? (OPEN-D3-3)
method: pg_table_size, pg_indexes_size and pg_total_relation_size of every table and index after the volume load and before its deletion; pg_column_size and octet_length of kb.segment.text and kb.rendition.canonical_text. PostgreSQL 18.6 (Ubuntu 18.6-1.pgdg24.04+2), pg_textsearch 1.5.1, vector 0.8.7, on the project-local cluster (just db-up; socket build/pg/run, port 5440, pg_textsearch preloaded); DDL applied and rows written as the NOLOGIN non-superuser cs_s6_app (SET ROLE) in cs_spike_s6 cloned from cs_template; psycopg 3.3.6 (binary), pgvector-python 0.5.1, spike venv checked against the lock (`uv sync --locked --check`: no changes) before the final run; free disk 109G at start, 106G at end.

agents.separation: coordinator brief; wrote only code/s6_*, code/s6*.py/.sql, results/s6/, records/s6.*

results.name: segment_text_bytes
results.note: stored bytes (raw 421588); 13.2% of kb.segment with its indexes; 0.41% of the four schemas at volume

results.name: canonical_text_bytes_stored
results.note: stored bytes, TOAST-compressed (raw 66645); raw segment text is 6.3x the raw canonical text (every level of the tree, sentences included, repeats it)

results.name: segment_text_per_unit_bytes
results.note: segment text bytes per author unit on the four pages (124 units) vs observation payload bytes per volume unit (11608 at 40 observations per unit)

conclusion: Segment text is small beside what a run writes: about 2.6 kB per author unit against about 11.6 kB of observation payload per unit, 0.4% of the database at run scale. It is 6.3 times the raw canonical text, because every tree level and every sentence repeats it; the BM25 kinds alone are 74 kB on the four pages. OPEN-D3-3 stays closed by mechanism, with the sizes to support keeping the column.
